## What it is

Rear bay that bolts to the housing backplate and holds an Arduino UNO R4 WiFi with an ElectroCookie terminal shield stacked on it. Removable cover, matrix-lead slot, capacitor channel, and strain-relief exits for the 5 V lead and the arcade-button wires.

## Design notes

- Prints mating-face down, cavity up. Standoffs, nut pockets, the crowned port roofs and the vents all build upward, so the part needs no supports. The bay is 60 mm tall; that is still well under the CR-10's 400 mm.
- Board origin (USB/barrel edge, analog edge) sits at housing `(-40, 10)`. The shield uses that same corner. Mounting holes are the official ABX00087 T8 coordinates; the shield drawing does not dimension its own holes.
- Standoffs are 6 mm tall with a blind Ø4.1 mm hole, 5 mm deep, for a ruthex RX-M3Sx4.0 insert. An M3×18 screw at each hole passes through the shield, the 11 mm header gap and the Uno into the insert.
- USB-C and the barrel jack are crowned openings in the connector wall, lined up on the Uno. The crown is 45 degrees. A slot open for the full 60 mm would take that wall out, and a flat roof over a 14 mm hole sags.
- The 5 V notch stays on the wiring-bay wall, open at the rim, with its zip-tie eye. The floor slot still hits the housing's upper-right window. A zip-tie bar closes the upper end of that slot; the lower 6 mm stays open for the matrix leads.
- Arcade-button leads (red D8, white D4, grounds) leave through a rim-open notch in the bottom wall, at housing X = 40, and tie off on the eye just inside.

## Don't

- Don't lower the shell below housing Y = -16. The original base-mount pillars occupy the backplate up to Y = -20.
- Don't replace the port crowns with a flat bridge. A 14 mm flat roof sags; the 45 degree crown is the printable cap.
- Don't run the heat-set hole through the floor. The insert needs the 1 mm of plastic under it.
- Don't drop `tb_wire_clearance` below 15 mm. That is the room above the terminals.
